rows.why: S1 covers several list items: the BOM (2), the header (5), row order (1) and CRLF on every line (3). Item 5 is the closest because the scenario is about the header and the rows that follow it. Its header string matches exactly, and the picks for items 1, 2 and 3 also match the scenario.

The most specific thing S2 settles is how the creation time is written, which is item 6. The scenario wants a UTC date only (YYYY-MM-DD), but the pick writes the full ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds. Item 11 (empty field for a missing title) agrees, but no item asks how status labels are shown.
Item 4 asks what an empty list produces. The pick returns the BOM and the header line only, which is what S3 expects.

Item 12 asks how fields with commas, quotes or line breaks are escaped. 'Quotes fields per RFC 4180 and doubles inner quotes' covers the separator cases. It doesn't say whether a title that starts or ends with a space gets quoted (RFC 4180 doesn't require that), or whether plain fields are left unquoted, so it can't be checked against the whole scenario.

Item 12 also asks whether values starting with =, +, - or @ are guarded against formula injection. The pick explicitly does not neutralise leading formula characters, but S5 requires a leading single quote.

S6 combines items 7 (unknown status), 8 (bad numbers), 9 (filled greater than openings) and 10 (invalid date). Item 7 is the closest single match. Each of those picks throws an Error naming the requisition id, which is what S6 expects.
